newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says stops importing foreign workers.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says stops importing foreign workers.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Saturday the government had stopped issuing permits allowing companies to import foreign labour.

He told the general assembly of his political party, the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), that companies needing foreign labour could recruit illegal immigrants held temporarily at immigration depots before deportation.
"We have frozen all permits for foreign workers. If companies want them they can go to the (immigration) depots," Anwar said in a speech at UMNO's three-day annual assembly which ends on Saturday.
But Anwar said Malaysia would continue to depend on resident foreign labour as the booming economy was short of labour.

Foreign workers in Malaysia are concentrated in menial work. Popular resentment of foreign workers has risen in recent months after a spate of ugly incidents involving foreign workers and Malaysians, including fights between Bangladeshi workers and villagers.
Anwar said there were 750,000 foreign workers with work permits in the country and a million more who work illegally.
Of those with valid permits, 306,000 were Indonesians and 117,500 Bangladeshis. The rest were mainly from the Philippines, Thailand, Pakistan, India, Sri Lanka and Burma.
Anwar denied suggestions that crime was rampant among foreign workers.
He said of 10,623 serious crimes committed in Malaysia this year up to August, only 628 were carried out by foreign workers. Only 2,167 of 70,798 cases of property-related crimes involved foreigners.
